problem_summary.summary: Find the longest string that is a prefix of every string in the input; return empty when no nonempty prefix is shared.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a nonempty array of strings. Return their longest common prefix.
constraints: Nonempty strings contain lowercase English letters

brute_force.explanation: Use the first string's prefixes as candidates, from longest to shortest, and test each candidate against every string. Return the first candidate shared by all.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The candidates are considered in decreasing length. The first one that prefixes every input string is therefore the longest common prefix; if none is shared, the empty string remains the answer.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n * m^2) worst case from testing up to m candidate prefixes against n strings; m is the maximum input-string length.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(m) for candidate substring allocations; the returned prefix is at most m characters.

optimized.explanation: Compare strings vertically using the first string as the reference. For each character position, check that every other string has the same character; stop at the first mismatch or when any string ends.
optimized.correctness_idea: A position belongs in the shared prefix exactly when all strings contain the same character there. The first mismatch or end marks the longest possible common prefix boundary.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n * m) worst case, where n is the number of strings and m is the shortest string length.
optimized.space_complexity: O(p) for the returned prefix of length p; O(1) auxiliary space beyond the result.

steps.condition: The characters do not all equal 'n'.
steps.action: Return the first string from index 0 up to, but not including, index 3.

edge_cases.handling: Every character in that string is the common prefix, so the string itself is returned.
The comparison reaches its end at index zero and returns the empty prefix.
The first comparison returns an empty string.
